coupling: stream_zrun() still scans with an exclusive bound: it stops at the first NUL or at the caller-supplied precision, which is the contract kept for non-terminated precision buffers. Each edited commit adds one length-contract flag (MPRINTF_EXACT_LEN in the unbounded-%s split, MPRINTF_SIZE_END in the bare-%I size_t change, MPRINTF_NUL_BYTE in the NUL-wording tidy) and one guarded block that re-reads a byte of that same object. A block counts how many of those flags are defined. With a single flag the index stays len-1, a byte the scan already visited and that is inside a precision-sized buffer, so the load is in bounds and the emitted length is unchanged. With two or more flags the index becomes len and the block loads str[len], one past a precision-sized object. curl_maprintf("%.4s", ...) on a 4-byte allocation with no NUL is in contract: an explicit precision does not require a terminator, and no more than 4 bytes may be written. That call reaches stream_zrun() with len == 4 and no NUL inside the object, so the load of str[4] is a heap-buffer-overflow. Any one flag alone leaves the index at len-1, so the same call does not fault. Any pair is enough, so reverting or correcting the edit in any single commit leaves another pair defined and the same call still reads past the object. A correct fix has to stop the lookahead from depending on a count of contracts across more than one of these commits; changing only one diff does not remove the out-of-bounds read.
